findings.title: Device is cached before DB write, so a rejected device is admitted on retry
findings.body: tagDeviceUI calls localCache.SetDefault(key) before anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice. When CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached for a new device, the cache entry remains for 29 minutes. The next Authenticate for the same device hits the cache at line 83, TagDevice returns nil, and client.go therefore returns a successful identity. The configured limit is thus only enforced on the very first request from a process, after which the over-limit device is allowed in.

findings.title: Device-limit check is a non-atomic count-then-insert (TOCTOU)
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice does CountDevices in one DB session and then performs the INSERT/ upsert in a separate session without a transaction, lock, or unique-count constraint. Concurrent anonymous authentications (now synchronous in client.go, and potentially across multiple Grafana instances sharing the DB) can all observe count < deviceLimit and all insert, exceeding the limit. The limit is therefore not reliably enforced under parallel first-time devices.

findings.title: Anonymous authentication now blocks on synchronous DB tagging with no timeout
findings.body: Previously TagDevice ran in a goroutine with a 2-minute timeout on a background context and never blocked login. Now Authenticate synchronously calls TagDevice(ctx, ...) on the request path: every cache-miss anonymous request waits for a COUNT plus INSERT/UPDATE, and a slow/hung database can stall or, via request-context cancellation, abort authentication/tagging. This adds DB latency/load to anonymous page/API loads and removes the panic-recovery/timeout isolation the async path had.

findings.title: Expired existing device is permanently rejected when limit is reached
findings.body: When count >= limit, CreateOrUpdateDevice delegates to updateDevice, which only updates rows whose updated_at is within the last 30 days (anonymousDeviceExpiration). A device returning after >30 days is not included in CountDevices (its slot is free), but updateDevice affects 0 rows and returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. It can never refresh updated_at, so it stays expired and is rejected until the 61-day cleanup deletes it, even though it should be treated as a (re-)new device subject only to the current count.

findings.title: New device_limit option is not declared in defaults/docs
findings.body: cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit reads auth.anonymous/device_limit, but the PR adds no entry to conf/defaults.ini (or configuration documentation). Operators have no discoverable, documented way to set the feature the PR introduces, and Grafana's config-documentation/defaults consistency checks expect new settings to be declared there.

findings.title: Frontend limit type does not match the value actually sent
findings.body: AnonymousDeviceLimit is a plain int64, so the backend always serializes anonymousDeviceLimit as a number (0 when unlimited). The frontend declares it as `number | undefined` in grafana-data/grafana-runtime and defaults it to undefined, implying undefined means unset/unlimited. Consumers checking `=== undefined` will never see that state from a real server; unlimited is indistinguishable in type from a ( nonsensical ) limit of 0 unless they know the backend convention.
